    <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","headline":"[Bug]: webRTC not working properly on ios device","articleBody":"### Capacitor Version 7.4.3\n\n**INTRODUCTION**\n\nHello from Australia!\n\nMy name is Scott and I'm using the sdk **@openai/agents-realtime** and I'm having a huge problem with it in the capacitor app.\n\nBasically it works perfectly on the android device, google chrome browser and safari browser but on the ios device i have a small bug that i cannot erradicate.\n\nBasically how the app works is that a webRTC is created on the client side and it streams audio from the client side to openAI when the client speaks into the microphone openAI replies back in audio. It's awsome.\n\n**THE PROBLEM**\n\nThe problem I'm having is that when the audio first starts to play on the ios device it stops then starts then stops and starts on the first play. After the first play, it works perfectly.\n\nThis is definately a capacitor bug because i can get it to work perfectly in the safari and chrome browsers and on an capacitor app on an android device but it malfunctions on the first audio play on a capacitor app on an ios device.\n\n**THE LIKELY CAUSE**\n\nThe reason for this error is because capacitor apps for ios use a special wrapper (WKWebView) that mimics safari and the reason this error doesn't occur in the safari browser is because safari's audio handling has been built to handle this situation but the wrappers (WKWebView) that are used in frameworks like capacitor haven't been just yet, let me explain this in more detail.......\n\nSafari (the full browser) runs in a long-lived WebKit process that usually has the AVAudioSession already active (or quickly activated) after a user gesture. When WebRTC/audio starts, Safari often has the route + sample rate “hot,” so first playback is smooth.\n\nWKWebView on the otherhand (the wrapper that capacitor and many others are using atm) starts cold and so first audio play from a webRTC will stop and start and stop and start a few times on first play as the audio sets up from scratch each time on first play. **_So to fix the error it would be pretty easy on your end because all you really need to do is pre-activate the AVAudioSession inside capacitor._**\n\n**RESOURCES**\n\nThe sdk is below but in the project I am giving you via github the sdk is provided via cdn so you don't have to install it but the documentation for this sdk is below if you still want to read it:\n\nhttps://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/voice-agents/quickstart/\n\nI made a youtube video showing you how it works on everything except ios device.\n\nhttps://youtu.be/EY5epJqta_0\n\nI have already made you a simple project in capacitor, javascript and html using this library from openAI and you can use this project to debug the problem with capacitor **only you will need to create your own openAI client secret key** from the openAI console here;\n\nhttps://platform.openai.com/api-keys\n\nAlso because the cdn sdk is using webRTC, the app must be hosted on a https local server not http so therefore **you will need to create the two certificates** to enable this using the unix comands below from the root directory:\n\n1) Install mkcert (once)\nbrew install mkcert\n\n2) Install the local root CA (once)\nmkcert -install\n\n3) Create a cert specifically for your IP\nmkcert -cert-file ip.pem -key-file ip-key.pem 123.456.78.9 (your ip address on your machine) \n\nI have already completed the imports for these two certificates so you just need to make them and keep them in the root directory.\n\ni have already made all the configurations for ios and android for you to run this project on your own device via xcode and android studio and I have already set up the capacitor.config and vite.config.js files only you will need to put your own ip address there as i have still got mine there.\n\nHere is the project I have built for you so you can use it to debug the issue:\n\nhttps://github.com/scottywm/capacitorTest.git\n\nTo run the project you need to use vite on port 5173, just run the command below from the route directory:\nnpx vite --port 5173\n\nIf you need help getting the project started and have other questions I'm happy to chat with you over a zoom meeting if you like. Just email me at scott_mcmahon@y7mail.com.\n\nPlease action this asap because i've been working on my app all year and im almost finished and now this bug in capacitor is a fatal flaw so please fix it.\n\n### Other API Details\n\n```Shell\n\n```\n\n### Platforms Affected\n\n- [x] iOS\n- [ ] Android\n- [ ] Web\n\n### Current Behavior\n\nThe capacitor app works perfectly on an android device and i can even get it to work perfectly in the chrome and safari browser but when I use capacitor to make it into an app it malfunctions on an ios device when the audio first starts playing. The first audio play on an ios device stops then starts then stops then starts. This is terrible!\n\n### Expected Behavior\n\nThe audio must play smoothly on both ios and android devices without stops and starts.\n\n### Project Reproduction\n\nhttps://github.com/scottywm/capacitorTest.git\n\n### Additional Information\n\nI've been working on this app for nine months staright now and this error is fatal so it must get fixed ASAP!!!","author":{"url":"https://github.com/scottywm","@type":"Person","name":"scottywm"},"datePublished":"2025-09-30T15:33:27.000Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"https://schema.org/CommentAction","userInteractionCount":2},"url":"https://github.com/8176/capacitor/issues/8176"}</script>

cold and so first audio play from a webRTC will stop and start and stop and start a few times on first play as the audio sets up from scratch each time on first play. **_So to fix the error it would be pretty easy on your end because all you really need to do is pre-activate the AVAudioSession inside capacitor._**\n\n**RESOURCES**\n\nThe sdk is below but in the project I am giving you via github the sdk is provided via cdn so you don't have to install it but the documentation for this sdk is below if you still want to read with capacitor **only you will need to create your own openAI client secret key** from the openAI console here;\n\nhttps://platform.openai.com/api-keys\n\nAlso because the cdn sdk is using webRTC, the app must be hosted on a https local server not http so therefore **you will need to create the two certificates** to enable this using the unix comands below from the root directory:\n\n1) Install cold and so first audio play from a webRTC will stop and start and stop and start a few times on first play as the audio sets up from scratch each time on first play. **_So to fix the error it would data-team-hovercards-enabled="true" class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body NewMarkdownViewer-module__safe-html-box__ZT1eD"><h3 dir="auto">Capacitor Version 7.4.3</h3>
<p dir="auto"><strong>INTRODUCTION</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Hello from Australia!</p>
<p dir="auto">My name is Scott and I'm using the sdk <strong>@openai/agents-realtime</strong> and I'm having a huge problem with it in the capacitor app.</p>
<p dir="auto">Basically it works perfectly on the android device, google chrome browser and safari browser but on the ios device i have a small bug that i cannot erradicate.</p>
<p dir="auto">Basically how the app works is that a webRTC is created on the client side and it streams audio from the client side to openAI when the client speaks into the microphone openAI replies back in audio. It's awsome.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>THE PROBLEM</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">The problem I'm having is that when the audio first starts to play on the ios device it stops then starts then stops and starts on the first play. After the first play, it works perfectly.</p>
<p dir="auto">This is definately a capacitor bug because i can get it to work perfectly in the safari and chrome browsers and on an capacitor app on an android device but it malfunctions on the first audio play on a capacitor app on an ios device.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>THE LIKELY CAUSE</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">The reason for this error is because capacitor apps for ios use a special wrapper (WKWebView) that mimics safari and the reason this error doesn't occur in the safari browser is because safari's audio handling has been built to handle this situation but the wrappers (WKWebView) that are used in frameworks like capacitor haven't been just yet, let me explain this in more detail.......</p>
<p dir="auto">Safari (the full browser) runs in a long-lived WebKit process that usually has the AVAudioSession already active (or quickly activated) after a user gesture. When WebRTC/audio starts, Safari often has the route + sample rate “hot,” so first playback is smooth.</p>
<p dir="auto">WKWebView on the otherhand (the wrapper that capacitor and many others are using atm) starts cold and so first audio play from a webRTC will stop and start and stop and start a few times on first play as the audio sets up from scratch each time on first play. <strong><em>So to fix the error it would be pretty easy on your end because all you really need to do is pre-activate the AVAudioSession inside capacitor.</em></strong></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>RESOURCES</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">The sdk is below but in the project I am giving you via github the sdk is provided via cdn so you don't have to install it but the documentation for this sdk is below if you still want to read it:</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/voice-agents/quickstart/" rel="nofollow">https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/voice-agents/quickstart/</a></p>
<p dir="auto">I made a youtube video showing you how it works on everything except ios device.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://youtu.be/EY5epJqta_0" rel="nofollow">https://youtu.be/EY5epJqta_0</a></p>
<p dir="auto">I have already made you a simple project in capacitor, javascript and html using this library from openAI and you can use this project to debug the problem with capacitor <strong>only you will need to create your own openAI client secret key</strong> from the openAI console here;</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://platform.openai.com/api-keys" rel="nofollow">https://platform.openai.com/api-keys</a></p>
<p dir="auto">Also because the cdn sdk is using webRTC, the app must be hosted on a https local server not http so therefore <strong>you will need to create the two certificates</strong> to enable this using the unix comands below from the root directory:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">Install mkcert (once)<br>
brew install mkcert</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Install the local root CA (once)<br>
mkcert -install</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Create a cert specifically for your IP<br>
mkcert -cert-file ip.pem -key-file ip-key.pem 123.456.78.9 (your ip address on your machine)</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">I have already completed the imports for these two certificates so you just need to make them and keep them in the root directory.</p>
<p dir="auto">i have already made all the configurations for ios and android for you to run this project on your own device via xcode and android studio and I have already set up the capacitor.config and vite.config.js files only you will need to put your own ip address there as i have still got mine there.</p>
<p dir="auto">Here is the project I have built for you so you can use it to debug the issue:</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/scottywm/capacitorTest.git">https://github.com/scottywm/capacitorTest.git</a></p>
<p dir="auto">To run the project you need to use vite on port 5173, just run the command below from the route directory:<br>
npx vite --port 5173</p>
<p dir="auto">If you need help getting the project started and have other questions I'm happy to chat with you over a zoom meeting if you like. Just email me at <a href="mailto:scott_mcmahon@y7mail.com">scott_mcmahon@y7mail.com</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Please action this asap because i've been working on my app all year and im almost finished and now this bug in capacitor is a fatal flaw so please fix it.</p>

class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body NewMarkdownViewer-module__safe-html-box__ZT1eD email-format"><div class="email-fragment">Thanks mate.
The issue is that when the webrtc is first established the track for the audio coming in is mixed momentarily with the audio going out.

So essentially what is happening the audio coming in from open AI is getting sent back out so the ai model replys to itself in an endless loop that lasts for between 5 to 10 seconds.

I don't think is issue has anything to do with the Avaudiosession anymore.

This is indeed a bug with either capacitor, webkit or even Wkwebview.

I have submitted the bug to apple and webkit and pray someone fixes it.

This is a huge flaw that will hurt capacitor and it's reputation in the next few years because ai is really advancing and apps are going to use streaming features much more over time as AI gets more advanced.

The reason why no one noticed this issue earlier was because no one was needing to use capacitor for streaming as they would normally use a native framework for such and app or even react native.

Personaly I like capacitor because it's more easy, flexible and enables us to reuse our web code to make an app. This is an awesome advantage.

However if we want capacitor to be able to compete with the native frameworks we need to get on top of these types of issues.</div></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex
